annotation.authors_or_issuer: van der Horst, M.; Puzio, A.
key_provisions_or_claims: Relational sexual self should be understood both ontologically and at the level of desire, possibly enriched by Japanese philosophy.
Frictionless sex robot design is not neutral and may create narcissistic echo chambers.
Designing for friction requires consent, safeword with immediate shutdown, and boundary memory safeguards.
Open question whether human-human sexual norms should transfer to human-robot interactions or a distinct framework is needed.
Calls for intersectional, interdisciplinary research on queering sex robots.
annotation.summary_en: Reply commentary in Philosophy & Technology responding to Shimizu and Ooka on queering sex robots. It defends a relational ontology of the sexual self and endorses consent, safeword and trauma-sensitivity safeguards for 'designing for friction', and asks whether human-human sexual ethics should transfer to sex robots.
annotation.title_clean: The Relational Sexual Self, Interhuman Sexuality & Sex Robot Ethics
annotation.title_en: The Relational Sexual Self, Interhuman Sexuality & Sex Robot Ethics
